what: Grouped kernel v3: 32-bit word loads, 8 nibbles per load
change: One int32 load now yields eight nibbles, replacing four byte loads for the same data. The eight nibbles of a word accumulate in a single expression rather than eight separate memory-touching chains.

result.via: bn=4, bw=32 words per tile, 1 warp

readings.instruction_count_matters_more_than_byte: v2 gained 27% by removing 8x redundant scale loads that were only 1.6% of traffic. v3 gained 16% by cutting load instructions 4x while touching the same bytes. Both point the same way: this kernel is instruction-bound, not bandwidth-bound, at 68.8 GB/s of a 243.8 ceiling.
readings.still_short: 68.8 projects to 20.1 tok/s, just under Strata's 22.6. So after a day of work the kernel is at 89% of parity and cannot yet beat the baseline end to end. That is the honest position.

cumulative_today.note: measured under one method, on the same harness

pf (prefetch) staging for the next word while the current decodes
then the end-to-end wiring once parity is passed
